description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Once org.gradle.parallel and org.gradle.tooling.parallel are independent, the flag is redundant, so Gradle 10 simply ignores it. No action is required in Gradle 9.x; if you set it explicitly, you can remove it when upgrading to Gradle 10. Deprecation of starting external processes at configuration time with ExecOperations and Java/Groovy st

k outputs for binary compatibility. The new destinationDirectory output is optional, allowing task types compiled against an earlier Gradle version that override getDestinationDir() to continue supplying the destination through the legacy output. In Gradle 10, destinationDirectory will become the sole registered output. Task types overriding the legacy accessors require special care during this transition: An overridden getDestinationDir() takes precedenc
parallel to preserve backward compatibility. Relying on this implicit behavior is now deprecated. When org.gradle.parallel is enabled and org.gradle.tooling.parallel is not set explicitly during model building, Gradle emits a deprecation warning. In Gradle 10, the two properties will become independent, and enabling org.gradle.parallel without an explicit value for org.gradle.tooling.parallel during model building will be an error. To avoid the warning an
d prepare for Gradle 10, set org.gradle.tooling.parallel explicitly to either true or false , for example in gradle.properties : org.gradle.tooling.parallel=true Additionally, the transitional system property org.gradle.too
ling.parallel.ignore-legacy-default (used by some IDEs during sync to opt out of the legacy default) will no longer be honored in Gradle 10. Once org.gradle.parallel and org.gradle.tooling.parallel are independent, the flag is redundant, so Gradle 10 simply ignores it. No action is required in Gradle 9.x; if you set it explicitly, you can remove it when upgrading to Gradle 10. Deprecation of starting external processes at configuration time with 
d way to run a process at configuration time. Starting an external process at configuration time in any of the deprecated ways is already an error when the Configuration Cache is enabled. Because the Configuration Cache will be enabled by default in Gradle 10, Gradle now deprecates unsupported behaviors even when the Configuration Cache is not currently enabled. Migrate to one of the following, in order of preference: Move the process execution into a tas
ild Cache from build logic Enabling the Build Cache from build logic by mutating the start parameter, for example gradle.startParameter.buildCacheEnabled = true in a settings.gradle(.kts) file or init script, is now deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10. Whether the Build Cache is enabled is determined by the Gradle invocation ( --build-cache / --no-build-cache ) and the org.gradle.caching Gradle property, and is not intended to be overridden by bui
n in parallel, matching the behavior of tasks within a single build. As part of this change, a task consuming the outputs of a task in another build without declaring an explicit or implicit dependency is now deprecated. This will become an error in Gradle 10, matching the existing behavior for tasks in the same build. See Implicit dependencies between tasks for details and possible solutions. Deprecation of creating and copying StartParameter Starting in
 Gradle 10, constructing new instances of StartParameter will no longer be permitted. It was never intended to be instantiated or copied by build logic, but the public no-argument constructor and the newInstanc
arameter.newInstance() StartParameter.newBuild() The existing StartParameter instance for a build may be obtained via Gradle.getStartParameter() instead of constructing or copying one. Deprecation of Signature as a Configuration artifact Starting in Gradle 10, Signature will no longer implement PublishArtifact . The following methods inherited from PublishArtifact have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10: getName() / setName(String) getExtens
 via Signature must be updated. The shouldBePublished() method inherited from PublishArtifactInternal has also been deprecated for removal. As a result, a Signature will no longer be permitted directly as an artifact of a Configuration . Starting in Gradle 10, the Signing Plugin will no longer create the signatures configuration or automatically add Signature instances to it. The getConfiguration() and setConfiguration(Configuration) methods on SigningExt
ension have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10. Creating a configuration named signatures before the signing plugin is applied is now also deprecated. Deprecation of constructing Signature instances Starting in Gradle 10, manually constructing a Signature instance will no longer be permitted. All public constructors for this type have been deprecated for removal. To sign files, use the sign methods on the Sign task, 
or use the sign methods on SignOperation . Deprecation of getSignatures() and getSingleSignature() on SignOperation The getSignatures() and getSingleSignature() methods on SignOperation have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10. Use getFilesToSign() and getSignatureFiles() instead. Deprecation of signing files with a classifier The following methods that accept a classifier alongside files to sign have been deprecated and w
ill be removed in Gradle 10: Sign.sign(String, File…​) SignOperation.sign(String, File…​) SigningExtension.sign(String, File…​) The classifier argument is ignored during signing and does not influence the resulting signature fi
.api.Named . Passing any other type to Attribute.of(String, Class) — or declaring an unsupported type as the type parameter of an AttributeCompatibilityRule or AttributeDisambiguationRule — now emits a deprecation warning and will become an error in Gradle 10. The most common case is a plain Java Enum that does not implement Named . Such types often work at first but fail later during dependency resolution, publishing, or configuration cache serialization
lugin. To fix builds affected by this deprecation, upgrade the Kotlin Gradle Plugin to 2.1.0 or later. KGP 2.1.0 and newer do not use a plain enum for this attribute and are unaffected. Like the general case, this deprecation will become an error in Gradle 10. See the variant attributes documentation for the full set of supported attribute value types. Deprecation of macOS on AMD64 macOS AMD64 (Intel) is deprecated as a supported platform and will be remo
ved from the supported platforms in Gradle 10. macOS 27 runs on Apple Silicon only, and the OpenJDK macOS/x64 port is deprecated for removal , so JDK 27 and newer are not available for the platform. Gradle is therefore no longer tested on macOS 
AMD64 with Java 27 or newer. To prepare for Gradle 10, move your builds to macOS AArch64 (Apple Silicon). Upgrading from 9.6.0 and earlier Potential breaking changes Resilient sync reports failed operations Tooling API clients that query models through 
ne (or the equivalent None type). Feature previews Opt into improved dependency resolution ordering A new feature preview, ENHANCED_GRAPH_ORDERING , is available to opt into new dependency resolution ordering behavior that will become the default in Gradle 10. With this feature preview enabled, Gradle will use a standard breadth-first ordering when using the DEFAULT sort order. Gradle may optionally be configured to return artifacts sorted topologically, 
sing the CONSUMER_FIRST sort option, which sorts artifacts earlier than those they depend on. As usual, the DEPENDENCY_FIRST ordering is the reverse of the CONSUMER_FIRST ordering. Notably, unlike the existing sorting methods, all sorting options in Gradle 10 will ignore constraint edges when traversing the resolved graph. You can enable this feature preview in your settings.gradle.kts : // settings.gradle.kts enableFeaturePreview("ENHANCED_GRAPH_ORDERING
") Deprecations Deprecation of the software model The Gradle software model — including the model { } DSL, RuleSource plugins, and the native and JVM component types built on top of them — is deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10. This affects the following groups of public API types: The rule-authoring API in org.gradle.model : RuleSource , ModelMap , ModelSet , ModelElement , and the @Model , @Mutate , @Defaults , @Finalize
not be restored as its own type and is instead restored as the nearest standard type, losing any state or behavior the custom type adds. Referencing such a custom subtype from a task field or task action is now deprecated and will become an error in Gradle 10. To fix it, use a standard collection or map type instead of a custom subtype, and store any extra data in separate fields. See Custom Collection and Map Types for details. Upgrading from 9.5.0 and e
chy — now deprecated build.gradle.kts (root project) extra["foo"] = "hello" child/build.gradle.kts val foo: String? by project println(foo) // Resolved through hierarchy — now deprecated This implicit inheritance is deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10. Implicit hierarchy lookup creates hidden coupling between projects, makes builds harder to reason about (a typo silently resolves to an ancestor’s definition instead of failing), and is fundamentall
xtraInHierarchy(name) } child/build.gradle def findExtraInHierarchy(Project project, String name) { if (project == null) return null if (project.ext.has(name)) return project.ext.get(name) return findExtraInHierarchy(project.parent, name) } Opt into Gradle 10 behavior by disabling implicit lookup in parent projects Once you have addressed all related deprecations, you can use a feature preview to adopt the Gradle 10 behavior early. t of the properties task when invoked for subprojects. s() have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10: Project.getProperties() — calling getProperties() or accessing the properties property on a Project instance. Calling getProperties() (or accessing the properties property) on a build script, settin
d: processResources { filesMatching("plugin.yml") { expand( "version": project.version, "name": project.name ) } } Deprecation of Kotlin DSL delegated properties All Kotlin DSL property delegate extensions have been deprecated and will be removed in Gradle 10. ionality already provided by explicit APIs or other DSL sugar. e documentation for alternatives that are compatible with the Configuration Cache. input.message:
I didn't edit any project files. Everything I ran or wrote is in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sweetjp-DEV-git-repos-minecraft-mods-ModularPlanters/6f49c4e8-7367-4f98-89c4-f1e8a15d7175/scratchpad/`.

**1. Gradle 10 is not released.**
- `https://services.gradle.org/versions/current` returns `"version" : "9.8.2"` (built 2026-10-19), and `/versions/all` contains no 10.x entry at all, not even a milestone.
- Latest 9.x is 9.8.2. The newest pre-release is 9.9.0-rc-1 (2026-10-30). The 8.x line is still getting patches (8.14.6, 2026-10-08).
- Gradle 10 changes that matter for this build, from https://docs.gradle.org/9.8.2/userguide/upgrading_version_9.html and upgrading_version_8.html:
  - **Groovy space-assignment:** the generated `propertyName value` methods "will be removed in Gradle 10, and both `propertyName value` and `propertyName(value)` will stop working unless the explicit method `propertyName` is defined."
    - The user's change from `url "..."` to `url = "..."` fixes exactly this.
    - Other spots in build.gradle are method calls, not space-assignment, so they stay valid: `programArgument '--nogui'`, `systemProperty ...`, `srcDir`, `exclude`, `from`, `expand`, `inputs.properties`.
  - **Configuration cache:** "the Configuration Cache will be enabled by default in Gradle 10". Starting external processes at configuration time the old ways is deprecated. The build already enables configuration cache and uses `providers.exec`, which is the supported way.
  - **`org.gradle.tooling.parallel`:** in Gradle 10 it becomes independent of `org.gradle.parallel` (details in section 3).
  - **Other removals in 10:**
    - `Project.getProperties()`. The build uses `hasProperty`/`property`, not this.
    - `DomainObjectCollection.findAll(Closure)`.
    - Kotlin DSL delegates.
    - `buildNeeded`/`buildDependents`.
    - `archives` configuration.
    - `Wrapper.getAvailableDistributionTypes()`.
    - Multi-string dependency notation.
    - `-P` toolchain properties (use `-D` instead).
    - macOS Intel dropped.
  - **Java requirement:** the 9.8.2 compatibility page says "A JVM version between 17 and 27 is required to execute Gradle." I found no published Gradle 10 JVM minimum.

**2. Both commands passed with no deprecation warnings.** Gradle 9.8.2 ran on JVM 25.0.4.
- `./gradlew help --warning-mode all --stacktrace`: the full output is 22 lines. The only notices are `Parallel Configuration Cache is an incubating feature.` and `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 587ms`. Configuration was fresh (no cache entry), so any deprecations would have shown.
- `./gradlew build --dry-run --warning-mode all`: output is the same incubating notice, then "configuration cache cannot be reused because file 'build.gradle' has changed", the task list all SKIPPED, and `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 564ms`. No deprecations.
- I also ran `./gradlew tasks --all --no-configuration-cache --warning-mode all`: zero "deprecat" or "warning" lines.
- **Wrapper:** the wrapper jar's sha256 (`7d3a4ac4...`) matches neither the published 9.2.1 jar (`423cb469...`) nor the 9.8.2 jar (`3b8a2577...`). It still launches 9.8.2, but `./gradlew wrapper` would regenerate `gradlew` and the jar to match.
- **ModDevGradle deprecation:** issue https://github.com/neoforged/ModDevGradle/issues/337 (open) reports "The DomainObjectCollection.findAll(Closure) method has been deprecated ... scheduled to be removed in Gradle 10." It did not appear in these runs. It may only show on other tasks such as IDE sync or the run tasks; that is a guess, I did not test those.

**3. Both properties are real, but `org.gradle.tooling.parallel` does not replace `org.gradle.parallel`.**
- `org.gradle.tooling.parallel` (build_environment page, https://docs.gradle.org/9.8.2/userguide/build_environment.html): "Since 9.4.0.     - Other spots in build.gradle are method calls, not space-assignment, so they stay valid: `programArgument '--nogui'`, `systemProperty ...`, `srcDir`, `exclude`, `from`, `expand`, `inputs.properties`.

    - `archives` configuration.
    - `Wrapper.getAvailableDistributionTypes()`.
    - Multi-string dependency notation.
    - `-P` toolchain properties (use `-D` instead).
